def: A language model placed in a loop that it controls: it reads its context, chooses a tool call or a final answer, observes the result and repeats until done or stopped.
The cycle of observe, think and act that an agent repeats, modelled as a state machine with terminal states Done and Stopped.
A structured request, with an id, tool name and arguments, that the model emits and your code executes before returning the result as an observation.
A system where your code fixes the sequence of steps and models only fill in individual steps, so every path can be enumerated and tested.
The fact that a task needing n steps succeeds with probability roughly p to the power n, so small per-step failure rates produce large end-to-end failure rates.
A pattern in which one call plans subtasks at run time, worker calls handle them (often in parallel) and a final call combines the results.
A pattern in which one call drafts, another judges against criteria, and rejected drafts return with feedback for another attempt up to a round limit.
An open standard that lets AI applications (hosts) connect through clients to servers exposing tools, resources and prompts using JSON-RPC.
A small protocol for remote calls in JSON with requests (id and method), responses (matching id with result or error) and notifications (no id, no reply).
Replacing older parts of the transcript with a short summary or stubs so the context stays within a size bound while the run continues.
A unique string sent with a side-effecting request so that a repeated request returns the stored result instead of repeating the action.
A retry policy whose delay before retry a is min(cap, base times 2 to the power a), giving a struggling service time to recover.
Randomness added to retry delays so that many clients do not retry at the same instant and cause a retry storm.
A persisted snapshot of an agent run's state after a step, allowing a crashed run to resume instead of restarting.
Detecting that an agent is repeating actions or making no progress, for example by counting identical tool-call signatures in a recent window.
The recording of one agent run as a tree of spans, each describing a model call, tool call or check with timing, inputs, outputs and status.
The probability that all k independent runs of a task succeed, p to the power k, a measure of consistency rather than capability.
A grouping of tools by worst-case misuse, from read-only through reversible and consequential writes to privileged actions, each with a default policy.
The maximum damage a misbehaving agent can do before it is stopped, bounded by rate limits, scoped credentials, reversibility and detection time.
An isolated environment, with restricted filesystem, network, CPU and memory, in which untrusted or model-written code runs.
An agent benchmark of real GitHub issues where a patch counts as resolving the issue only if the fix's fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests all pass.
The code around a model that makes it an agent (loop, tools, prompts, context management); agent results measure model and scaffold together.
The length of task, measured in skilled-human time, that a model completes with a given success rate (usually 50%).
A language model that plays the user in an agent evaluation, with a persona and a hidden goal, so conversational tasks can be repeated.
Judging an agent trial by the final state of its environment, such as database rows or passing tests, rather than by its words or exact steps.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall of an agent's tool calls matched against the calls a correct solution needs.
Total spend on an agent's attempts divided by the number of tasks it completed successfully.
